‘The receptors for interleukin-3 (IL-3) and granulo
ceyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF)
consist of two polypeptides each belonging to a new
class of molecules referred to as the hemopoietin recep-
tor family. When expressed alone, receptor polypep-
tides of this family often bind their respective factors
with lower affinity than the receptors identified in
whole cells. Despite the lack of structural evidence for
any enzymatic activity of the receptor polypeptides,
both IL-3 and GM-CSF stimulate tyrosine phosphory!-
ation of multiple intracellular substrates. We investi-
gated IL-3 and GM-CSF receptor structure and signal-
ing in a myeloid cell line, FDC-P1, which is dependent
‘on either IL-3 or GM-CSF for growth. Antiphospho-
tyrosine antibodies were used to immunoprecipitate
tyrosine-phosphorylated proteins from ™P-labeled
cells or to probe immunoblots. Both IL-3 and GM-CSF
‘stimulated the phosphorylation of a similar pattern of
polypeptides on tyrosine. One tyrosine phosphorylated
polypeptide migrated with M,= 135,000 and increased
to 150,000 over a period of 10 min following stimula-
tion of cells with IL-3 or GM-CSF. The M, = 135,000-
150,000 polypeptide phosphorylated in response to IL
3. was shown to be primarily the Aic-2A polypeptide,
the low affinity IL-3 receptor. Phosphatase treatment
showed that the dramatic IL-3-induced shift in appar-
ent molecular weight from M, = 125,000 in unstimu-
ated cells was entirely due to phosphorylation. The
closely related receptor, Aic-2B, was also tyrosine
phosphorylated in response to IL-3, although toa lesser
extent than Aic-2A. Treatment with GM-CSF resulted
in tyrosine phosphorylation of the Aic-2B polypeptide
exclusively. It was intriguing that GM-CSF treatment
did affect the mobility of the Aic-2A polypeptide on
polyacrylamide gels. Together, these results suggest
that the Aic-2A polypeptide is part of the IL-3 receptor
‘complex, but not the GM-CSF receptor. In contrast,
the Aic-2B polypeptide is a component of the GM-CSF
receptor, but it can also be utilized in an IL-8 receptor.

‘The two hemopoietic growth factors, IL-3* and GM-CSF
have some overlapping activities such as stimulation of the
progenitors of neutrophils, macrophages, megakaryocytes, eo:
‘inophils, and basophils. However, there are also differences;
IL-3 has a generally broader spectrum of target cells that
includes primitive hemopoietic stem cells and mast cells while
only GM-CSF affects mature neutrophils. Both have pleio-
tropic effects, stimulating the growth, differentiation, and
survival of thei targets. Two components of the receptor for
rouse IL-3 have been cloned. One is referred to as Aic-28
(toh, et al, 1990) and the other as SUT-1 (Hara and Miya-
ima, 1992) and both bind IL-3 with very low affinity. SUT-1L
‘encodes a polypeptide that cen be cross-linked to murine TL
3, having @ molecular mass of approximately 70 kDa and has
been designated the a subunit of that receptor (Hara and
‘Miyajima, 1992; Duronio etal, 1992). Aic-2A encodes a 12!
kDa polypeptide that can also be cross-linked to IL-3 and is
designated the ¢ subunit. A second mouse polypeptide closely
related to Aic-2A (1% homology), but having no known
binding function has also been cloned (Gorman et al, 1990,
Hayashida et al, 1990) and is referred to as Aic-2B. Recent
reports have provided evidence that Aic-2B forms part of the
murine GM-CSF (Kitamura et al, 19914) and IL-5 receptors
(Devos et al, 1991), while also being able to associate with
SUT-1 to form « functional IL-3 receptor (Hara and Miya:
jima, 1992),
